reason: Prior TB runs were slow, but they do not isolate transpose cost. A tiled NEON transpose is a distinct, correctness-checkable way to test whether conversion affects the full call. Four-step unrolling has a clear loop-control hypothesis, though earlier two-step unroll results did not promote and do not establish that unrolling helps. The 288-byte scratch stride is distinct from the measured 272-byte layout, but has no supplied cache evidence and adds 16 KiB. The proposed K-pair schedule may overlap the previously measured two-step unroll, so verify the instruction schedule before testing. TA has correct pointer mapping but adds timed conversion while retaining both generated packing paths. Half-band packing adds traversal and repacking complexity and resembles a prior unpromoted traversal. Fused transpose repeats A-tile transpose work across 16 column panels, making it the weakest proposal. All options require full correctness checks, including tails and bounds; no proposal has measured benefit in this board.
